title: Contextual playbook snapshots for escalations (PD/Slack integration)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On-call responders often lack the immediate context they need when PagerDuty or Slack triggers an escalation. Current incident notifications include a link to a runbook, traces, and logs, but responders must assemble the right log slices, trace spans, and metric deltas manually. This slows TTR and increases cognitive load.

Goal: When an escalation fires (PD or Slack incident channel creation), automatically capture and attach a 'playbook snapshot' to the notification. A playbook snapshot is a curated bundle of context tailored to the alert: relevant trace spans (root span + related downstream spans), a time-windowed log slice (−2m/+5m around alert time filtered by top N services), key metric deltas (p50/p95/err rate compared to a 30m baseline), and the runbook section(s) most likely to help for that alert class. This snapshot should appear inline in Slack messages and as an attachment/annotation on PagerDuty incidents, and be attached to the postmortem draft created by the postmortem automation flow.

Scope: PD/Slack hooks, trace selection heuristics, log pipeline filters, snapshot serialization, attachment/annotation UI surface, postmortem draft enrichment. Does not include full playbook authoring (handled by docs team) or multi-tenant RBAC beyond existing PD/Slack integration permissions.
acceptance_criteria: When a PD escalation is created for alert type X, Payload contains a playbook_snapshot URL pointing to the snapshot artifact stored in internal object store
When a Slack incident thread is created via alertbot, the message includes an expand/collapse playbook snapshot block summarizing traces/logs/metrics and link to full snapshot
Snapshot generation completes within 8s for P0/P1 alerts (goal) and within 20s for lower priorities
Postmortem automation attaches the same snapshot link to the generated postmortem draft and includes top 3 candidate root causes inferred from traces/logs
Access controls honor existing PD/Slack integration scopes; no secrets are leaked to public channels
success_metrics: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for incidents with playbook snapshot reduced by >=20% in first 6 weeks
% of PD incidents with a snapshot successfully generated >= 95%
Operator satisfaction score (internal survey) for on-call context >= 4.0/5 after rollout
design_notes: Snapshot model: small JSON manifest + signed pointer to an immutable S3 object with attached artifacts (trace ids, log query, metric deltas)
Trace selection heuristic: start from alert's span tags (service, trace_id) then include parent/child spans up to 3 hops and top 5 spans by duration; annotate with sampled logs references
Log slice: leverage existing metrics/log pipeline to produce prefiltered slices using service and request_id where available; store compressed NDJSON in object store for quick preview
Metric delta calc: compute p50/p95 and error-rate delta vs 30m baseline using metrics pipeline (precompute via streaming window where possible)
PD annotation: use PagerDuty 'links' and 'annotations' fields to attach summary + secure URL; fallback to a short payload if external network blocked
Slack UI: use blocks API to present a collapsed summary and a 'View snapshot' secure link; respect channel privacy and disable full artifact preview in #public channels
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated: start with internal teams only. 2) Runbook mapping: use a small mapping table from alert rule -> runbook sections. 3) Canary PD integration for 3 SRE teams for 2 weeks. 4) Expand to all PD escalation policies after 4 weeks if error rates low. 5) Postmortem enrichment on by default for Canary teams; opt-in later. Metrics and logs retention follow existing policies.
